datasets.name: Norwegian Mass Movements Database
datasets.source: Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE)
datasets.verbatim: The Norwegian Mass Movements Database (available from: https://nedlasting.nve.no/gis/, accessed on 20 December 2022) contained 84,768 reports at the time of writing, from the year 900 to 2022.

datasets.name: Jølster landslide inventory (120 manually mapped landslides)
datasets.verbatim: For verification of the results, we used a set of 120 manually mapped landslides [30].

datasets.name: Sentinel-1 imagery
datasets.verbatim: Images used included Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, as well as digital elevation model (DEM) and slope.

datasets.name: 10 m resolution Norwegian DEM
datasets.verbatim: Further, the 10 m resolution Norwegian DEM was used instead of the global 30 m resolution ALOS DEM, because the ALOS DEM does not cover Norway.

methods.name: U-Net CNN deep learning model
methods.summary: A U-Net convolutional neural network architecture implemented in Python (ArcPy, Keras, TensorFlow 2) for semantic segmentation of landslide pixels. It uses a sliding window approach on input image tiles (128x128 pixels) to classify pixels based on the surrounding patch context.
methods.verbatim: The locally trained GEE model is available: https://code.earthengine.google.com/91d0606e7797198754ec2a16d7333fb9 (accessed on 22 December 2022).

data_links.name: Locally trained Google Earth Engine (GEE) model

code_links.name: Locally trained Google Earth Engine (GEE) model
code_links.summary: A custom-trained model implemented and shared as a Google Earth Engine script/code repository.

availability.author_statement: Code availability statement present, with shared links. Data potentially retrivable from GEE script.

reproducibility_assessment: The landslide inventory is referenced and linked via the Norwegian Mass Movements Database, and other input datasets are accessible through public providers. The custom U-Net model code is provided via a persistent Google Earth Engine repository link.
